findings.situation: In a 2025 quarter the filer paid $1,200 in cash to a 17-year-old student babysitter and paid no other household workers. The help tells the filer to leave this pay out, so the answer is No, but the pay still meets the $1,000-per-quarter federal unemployment (FUTA) test.
findings.source_text: f1040s2 Schedule 2 (2025) p.1, line 9: "Household employment taxes. Attach Schedule H"
findings.why: Schedule H leaves out pay to workers under 18 only for the $2,800 social security and Medicare test. That pay still counts toward the $1,000 quarterly FUTA test. The help drops it from every test, so some filers who owe Schedule H tax answer No.

findings.situation: The filer paid their own 19-year-old child, their spouse or their parent $3,000 in 2025 to babysit or do housework. The filer answers Yes, but these wages are not counted for Schedule H.
findings.source_text: Question: "Did you ... pay any one of them $2,800 or more in 2025 ..."; f1040s2 (2025) p.1, line 9: "Household employment taxes. Attach Schedule H"
findings.why: Schedule H does not count wages paid to your spouse, your child under 21 or your parent (with narrow exceptions for a parent). The question and help never leave these people out, so the filer answers Yes and the return wrongly owes Schedule H tax.

findings.situation: A live-in carer received $1,500 in cash plus room and board worth $2,000 in 2025. Counting all of that as pay, the filer answers Yes.
findings.source_text: Question: "pay any one of them $2,800 or more"; Label: "cash wages of $2,800 or more"; f1040s2 (2025) p.1, line 9
findings.why: The Schedule H thresholds count only cash wages. The question asks about "pay" in general, so food, lodging and other non-cash pay get counted toward the thresholds.

findings.situation: In 2025 the filer paid $3,000 to a 17-year-old who is not a student, and household work is not that person's main job. The help leaves out only students, so the filer answers Yes.
findings.source_text: Help: "Do not count pay to a student who was under 18 in 2025."; f1040s2 (2025) p.1, line 9
findings.why: For the $2,800 test, Schedule H leaves out pay to any worker under 18 unless household work is their main job, whether or not they are a student. Limiting the exclusion to students brings in this case, which should not count.

locators: Schedule 2 (2025), line 9, "Household employment taxes. Attach Schedule H"
